title: Rheumatoid arthritis follow-up
what: The rheumatologist regularly checks how your treatment is working and whether it is causing harm. This helps protect your joints.
why: For everyone with rheumatoid arthritis: usually every 1 to 3 months at the start of treatment, and less often once the disease is quiet.
duration: the visit usually takes 20 to 30 minutes; test results in 1 to 3 days
tell_doctor: Which joints hurt and swell, and how long morning stiffness lasts
Side effects of medicines: nausea, rash, frequent infections

prepare.title: Tests
prepare.text: Blood is often drawn before the visit: a blood count, liver tests and inflammation markers. Ask which ones and when.

prepare.title: Diary
prepare.text: Write down how you felt between visits.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Take them as prescribed. Do not skip or stop them on your own.

bring: A list of medicines and doses
steps: The doctor asks about pain, stiffness and side effects
Assesses how active the disease is
Decides whether to keep or change the treatment
Sets the date of your next check
feel: Pressing on inflamed joints can hurt
A blood test is a quick needle prick
after: Have your tests on time. This protects you from side effects
Tell your doctor about your treatment before vaccinations and operations
Stay active and do the exercises your doctor allowed
red_flags: High fever, cough or shortness of breath during treatment: see a doctor urgently
Sudden weakness, bleeding or yellow skin: see a doctor urgently

faq.q: Can I stop treatment if my joints no longer hurt?
faq.a: No, not without your doctor. The disease can come back.
Many vaccines are fine and even recommended, but always check with your rheumatologist first.

reminders.text: Rheumatologist visit in 2 days. Do not forget your blood tests if the doctor asked for them.
